rounds.text: Jain Resource Recycling Ltd is demonstrating exceptional fundamental momentum, highlighted by a 70% compounded sales growth over three years and a 50% increase over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. This top-line expansion is matched by robust profitability, evidenced by compounded profit growth of 79% over three years and 66% in the trailing twelve months [E16, E17]. Furthermore, the business generates elite returns on capital, maintaining a 3-year median ROE of 37% and an ROCE of 19.98% that comfortably outstrips the sector benchmark of 5.75% [E10, E19]. Strategic expansion is already underway with copper anode production having commenced in March 2026 at an initial capacity of 800 metric tons per month, backed by guidance for copper volume growth to exceed 15% [E68, E75]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative at Rs -570 Cr in March 2026 and institutional holdings decreased [E26, E33]. Nevertheless, the company benefits from a strong sector tailwind in Metals & Mining with a score of +1.07, alongside a global procurement network spanning over 120 countries that firmly positions it within an emerging Indian recycling hub [E63, E70, E80].

Jain Resource Recycling Ltd carries substantial valuation and financial risks that are not fully supported by the underlying operational evidence, starting with a severe cash flow disconnect where operating cash flow collapsed to negative Rs 570 Cr in March 2026, resulting in a negative cash conversion ratio of -1.64x against reported profits [E25, E26]. This alarming cash burn coincides with a significant surge in total borrowings to Rs 1,253 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 817 Cr a year prior [E30], undermining the capital stability that its price-to-book multiple of 7.49x implies [E2]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is actively eroding, evidenced by foreign institutional holdings dropping to 1.23% alongside a negative institutional money flow reading [E33, E35], while the stock price languishes below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a relative strength rating of zero [E41, E42]. Operational fragility is additionally highlighted by a sharp quarterly operating margin contraction to 3% in March 2026 compared to 6% in the prior-year period [E22], coupled with vulnerability to external geopolitical shocks that disrupted shipping routes and constrained raw material supplies [E87]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong multi-year compounding growth in sales and profit alongside an expanding ROE and a favorable sector tailwind in metals and mining [E14, E16, E18, E61].

Conceded: operating cash flow was negative Rs 570 Cr in March 2026 and borrowings rose to Rs 1,253 Cr [E26, E30], but this cash drag occurred against a backdrop of deliberate inventory investments and temporary geopolitical shocks at Dubai port rather than structural failure [E87]. The bear's panic over balance sheet stability ignores that approximately INR 375 crores of the primary IPO issue was successfully utilized for debt repayment [E82], and management confirmed no fresh bank borrowings were availed in the last three to four months [E84]. While foreign institutional holdings declined, domestic institutional holdings expanded to 9.68% from 6.43%, reflecting institutional accumulation from domestic believers [E34]. The sharp quarterly margin dip in March 2026 to 3% [E22] was heavily distorted by a temporary confluence of one-time war headwinds and LME formula drops impacting EBITDA by INR 24,000 to INR 24,500 per ton [E78], rather than permanent operational degradation. Finally, lagging price momentum and moving averages [E41, E42] simply reflect transient sentiment overlooking strong fundamentals, such as copper volume growth projected beyond 15% and normalized EBITDA expected to stabilize between INR 30,000 and INR 32,000 per ton [E67, E68].

The bear's alarm over cash burn ignores the context of substantial capital deployment into major capacity expansions like the second copper anode furnace [E88], copper cathode phases [E89], and the wire rod project [E90], all backed by a healthy debt-to-equity ratio of 0.81x [E29] and zero fresh bank borrowings availed in the preceding three to four months [E84]. While institutional holdings adjusted [E33], domestic institutions aggressively increased their stake to 9.68% from 6.43% [E34], signaling strong local conviction in the multi-year top-line growth of 70% and profit growth of 79% [E14, E16]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative at Rs -570 Cr in March 2026 [E26] and foreign institutional holdings declined [E33], but these pressures stem directly from temporary geopolitical shipping disruptions in March rather than structural business decay [E77, E87]. Conceded: the stock trades below its moving averages with a zero relative strength rating [E41, E42], yet the company maintains a robust return on equity track record averaging over 30% [E13, E18, E49] and operates within a highly favorable metals and mining sector tailwind [E61, E63].

evidence.fact: The company expects copper volume growth to be in good double-digits with potential to go beyond 15%.
evidence.quote: So, on the growth side, I'd given my comment on this. And I mean, volumes depend upon many things but copper growth will be a good double-digit figure. It has potential to go beyond 15%.

evidence.fact: The company aims to reduce its stock to bring the working capital cycle down below 60 days.
evidence.quote: which will be our further policy to reduce the stock so that the working capital cycle which is around presently 66 days which should come down further below 60.

evidence.fact: India is emerging as a highly competitive global recycling hub supported by growth in domestic demand for non-ferrous metal.
evidence.quote: India, in particular, is emerging as a high-competitive global recycling hub, supported by favourable economics, strong processing capabilities, and growth in domestic demand for non-ferrous metal.

evidence.fact: The structural outlook for the recycling business is strengthened by an increasing focus on sustainability, circular economic practices, decarbonization, and supply-side constraints in mined metals.
evidence.quote: The increasing focus on sustainability, circular economic practices, decarbonization, and supply-side constraint in the mined metals continue to strengthen the structural outlook for recycling business.

evidence.fact: Copper recycling is increasing along with its application and the availability of scrap.
evidence.quote: but copper, because the recycling is increasing and the application is increasing and availability of scrap is increasing, therefore copper could be even higher.

evidence.fact: The company has finalized around six acres of land for a proposed shift of plastic recycling operations to a dedicated plant.
evidence.quote: The company has finalized around six acres of land for proposed shift of plastic recycling operations from the existing copper and lead recycling plants.

evidence.fact: The new dedicated plastic recycling unit will entail an estimated capex of around INR 15 crores.
evidence.quote: The new unit is targeted to become operational by quarter three financial year '27 and will entail an estimated capex of around INR15 crores, which will help us further strengthen our zero waste and circular economy model.

evidence.fact: The company's copper anode production commenced in March 2026 with an initial installed capacity of 800 metric ton per month.
evidence.quote: I am pleased to share that copper anode production has already commenced in March 2026 with an initial installed capacity of 800 metric ton per month.

evidence.fact: The company's EBITDA margin improved to 5.9% in FY26.
evidence.quote: Revenue grown by 48%, EBITDA increased by 53%, and EBITDA margin improved to 5.9%.

evidence.fact: Geopolitical disruptions from the Iran-Israel conflict impacted global shipping routes and increased logistics and fuel-related costs during March 2026.
evidence.quote: Secondly, the geopolitical disruptions arising from the Iran-Israel conflict impacted the global shipping routes and increasing logistic and fuel-related costs during March '26.

evidence.fact: The war situation impacted EBITDA by around INR 6,000 per ton, while the higher LME and drop in formula had an impact of approximately INR 18,000 to INR 18,500 per ton.
evidence.quote: So with respect to the war situation, EBITDA per ton got impacted for around INR6,000 per ton. And with respect to the higher LME and drop in formula, it was nearing approx INR18,000 to INR18,500 per ton.

evidence.fact: The company is utilizing around 65% of its installed copper capacity, close to 97% to 100% of lead capacity, and around 35% of aluminum capacity.
evidence.quote: So the copper, presently we are utilizing around 65% of the total installed capacity, while lead we are almost close to 97% to 100%, and aluminum is around 35% of the installed capacity.

evidence.fact: The company has sourcing capabilities across more than 120 countries.
evidence.quote: From a sourcing perspective, we continue to maintain one of the strongest global procurement networks in the industry, with sourcing capabilities across more than 120 countries, and domestic sourcing also improving steadily, supported by India's evolving recycling ecosystem, increased formalization, and EPR-led policy initiatives.

evidence.fact: Copper and copper alloy products contributed ~55% of total revenue during the quarter.
evidence.quote: As our strategic focus on the copper segment continues to strengthen, copper and copper alloy products contributed ~55% of total revenue during the quarter, compared to ~52% in the previous quarter and ~45% a year ago, reflecting the company’s continued emphasis on expanding its copper business in line with its stated guidance.

evidence.fact: Out of the primary IPO issue of around INR 500 crores, approximately INR 375 crores was utilized for debt repayment.
evidence.quote: Coming to IPO proceeds utilization during the year, from the primary issue of around INR500 crores, approximately INR375 crores was utilized towards repayment of the debts, while the balance amount was earmarked for general corporate purposes including the IPO expenses.

evidence.fact: The company's overall working capital cycle stood at around 66 days as of March 2026.
evidence.quote: As at March 2026, inventory days stood at approximately 62 days, debtor days stood at around 18 days and the creditor days stood at approximately 14 days. Accordingly, the overall working capital cycle stood at around 66 days.

evidence.fact: The company did not avail any fresh bank borrowings within the last three to four months.
evidence.quote: We didn't avail any of the fresh bank borrowings within last three to four months.

evidence.fact: Geopolitical disruptions from the Iran-Israel conflict impacted global shipping routes and increased logistics and fuel-related costs.
evidence.quote: Secondly, the geopolitical disruptions arising from the Iran-Israel conflict impacted the global shipping routes and increasing logistic and fuel-related costs during March '26.

evidence.fact: Dispatches for the Kuwait battery recycling venture have been temporarily delayed due to shipping route disruptions from the Iran-related geopolitical situation.
evidence.quote: However, due to disruption in shipping routes arising from Iran-related geopolitical situation, dispatches have been temporarily delayed.

evidence.fact: The company faced raw material supply constraints and container delays at Dubai port due to the geopolitical war.
evidence.quote: Yes, it is because of the geopolitical war. There is a supply of the raw material has been constrained and a lot of containers got stuck in Dubai port.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY27): The second copper anode furnace is expected to be commissioned during Q1 FY27.
evidence.quote: The second furnace with an additional 800 metric ton per month capacity is currently in the advanced stage of installation and is expected to be commissioned during quarter one financial year '27, taking the total anode capacity to 1,600 metric ton per month.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY27): The company expects phase one commissioning of copper cathode by Q2 FY27 and phase two by Q3 FY27.
evidence.quote: However, the project execution remains on track and we expect phase one commissioning by quarter two financial year '27 and phase two commissioning by quarter three financial year '27 respectively.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY27): The copper wire rod project is expected to be commissioned by August 2026.
evidence.quote: We expect commissioning by August 2026 with an installed capacity of 600 metric ton per month.
